title: 1967 Savoy College Reunion News
text:
act. Certainly it is commendable when we stop to remember the kindness of another because by it we express our appreciation and our awareness that someone has gone beyond the "call of duty" so to speak. It brings to someone may be happier for having passed your way. May you always have time, even for a very short time, to remember the kindnesses that have come your way, then say to that person for the memory. What a desolate place it must be when one lives without pleasant memories, but without pleasant memories.

As you return to your homes, may you take back with you a few memory plants to brighten the days ahead and to share with others that they too can be refreshed. This is my prayer for each of you.

Sincerely, Mrs. Annie Halse. Woodward

In order to print more interesting Savoy stories we are asking all of you to write us — tell something of yourself, your family, or some memory of the old Halsell College school days. These stories are interesting and may bring more material so that others will write us.

Write to your secretary, Mrs. G. R. Newby, P. O. Box 367, Bonham, Texas 75418.

JUDGE J. G. CLIFT

It was reported at the reunion that Judge J. G. Clift, 85, of Duncan, Okla., passed away in the early part of June this year following surgery. He was always interested in the reunions.

June 24, 1967

Mr. Robert F. Hodges, Sup.
Savoy Indep. School Dist.
P. O. Box 190
Savoy, Texas

Dear Mr. Hodges:

I was deeply touched when I saw the tangible evidence of your school system and all the efforts they extended to make all the fine talent you have in your school beautifully demonstrated how much you all appreciated my gift to your school, and filled my heart. Of all we have given to Christian Education, etc., I felt this gift to your school was more appreciated than all in all. I will never forget that day.

Your new school building shows the result of intellectual thinking and planning. It is beautiful as well as functional — perfect in every detail and from every angle.

Thank you again.

Sincerely, Charles Storch Lips

Dear Newby:

I am unable to attend the Savoy ex-students reunion, I regret very much.

I wish each one an enjoyable day.

Very sincerely yours, Mrs. Annie Halsell Woodward
304 North Fourth St., Durant, Okla.

Shown on the front page are some of the welcoming decorations on the Savoy school blackboards.

CONTRIBUTIONS

Eva Lee Galley, Phoenix, Arizona, $5.00.

Madill, Oklahoma
July 8, 1967

To: Mrs. Charles Storch Lips:
Our Pleasure is Joys
Like Coming to the End
of a Perfect Day
The Visitation with Great People

SAVOY COLLEGE REUNION
Representing Ex-Students —
Their Relatives and Friends
Program Very Fine
Devotional Services — Singing —
Speaking — Inspirational — Cultured
and Trained Voices Outstanding
The Special Reading and Tribute by the Granddaughter of a
Great Man — Our Mr. Halsell
His School — His Character —
His Work — His Influence —
those that lives on — and on — Most Impressive and will linger in our thoughts — Truly a "Masterpiece".

The Son and Grandson of
Rosa Belle Allred Ayres
(A former student)
Affectionately, Earl E. Ayres
Ernest Earl Ayres

Dear Mrs. Newby:

I am unable to attend the Savoy ex-students reunion, I regret very much.

I wish each one an enjoyable day.

Very sincerely yours, Mrs. Annie Halsell Woodward
304 North Fourth St., Durant, Okla.
